mainEntity.name: Can a severely broken tooth always be saved with a crown?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily. Whether a crown can be placed on a broken tooth depends on how much healthy tooth structure remains and the condition of the root and surrounding bone. If the root is severely fractured or the supporting structures are significantly compromised, a crown may not be viable. Your dentist will assess the tooth thoroughly, including X-rays, before advising on whether a crown or an alternative treatment is the most suitable option for your situation.

mainEntity.name: Does getting a crown on a broken tooth hurt?

acceptedAnswer.text: The preparation and placement of a dental crown is typically carried out under local anaesthetic, which numbs the area so you should not feel pain during the procedure. Some patients experience mild sensitivity or discomfort in the tooth and surrounding gum for a few days after treatment, which usually settles. If you experience significant or prolonged pain following crown placement, it is advisable to contact your dentist so they can check that everything has settled as expected.

mainEntity.name: How long does a dental crown last on a broken tooth?

acceptedAnswer.text: With good oral hygiene and regular dental check-ups, a dental crown can last many years — often ten years or more. However, individual outcomes vary and depend on factors such as the material used, oral hygiene habits, diet, whether you grind your teeth, and the clinical conditions of the tooth at the time of placement. Your dentist will be able to advise you on how to care for your crown and what to expect in terms of longevity based on your specific circumstances.

mainEntity.name: What happens if I leave a broken tooth untreated?

acceptedAnswer.text: Leaving a broken tooth without professional assessment and treatment can allow bacteria to enter the exposed inner layers of the tooth, potentially leading to decay, infection, or abscess. The break may also worsen over time, particularly under normal biting forces, reducing the likelihood of being able to save the tooth. Some patients experience increased sensitivity or pain as the condition progresses. Whilst not every broken tooth requires urgent treatment, prompt dental assessment is generally recommended to understand the extent of the damage and the options available.

mainEntity.name: Can a crown be placed on a tooth that has had a root canal?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, a dental crown is often recommended following root canal treatment. Root canal treatment involves removing the pulp tissue from inside the tooth, which can leave the tooth more brittle and vulnerable to fracture. Placing a crown over the treated tooth helps to protect it and restore its function. The suitability of crowning a root-treated tooth will still depend on the amount of remaining natural tooth structure and the overall condition of the tooth and root.

mainEntity.name: Will my dental insurance or plan cover a crown on a broken tooth?

acceptedAnswer.text: Coverage for dental crowns varies considerably depending on the type of dental plan or insurance policy you hold. Some plans include restorative treatments as part of their coverage; others may require additional payment or have limits on the materials covered. It is advisable to check the terms of your specific plan before treatment. Your dental practice should also be able to provide a clear treatment plan and associated costs prior to proceeding, allowing you to make an informed decision.
